summary:
The longest run of 1s after flipping at most `k` zeros is the longest window containing at most `k` zeros. Grow
the window right, counting zeros; when the count exceeds `k`, advance the left edge until a zero leaves. O(n).

question.md:
Turn at most `k` zeros of `status` into ones. Return the longest run of consecutive ones you can get.

- **n up to 10⁵.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- `k = 0`: the longest existing run of 1s.
- `k` at least the number of zeros: the whole log.
- All zeros: the answer is `min(k, n)`.

think.md:
**Which zeros should we patch?** Patching a zero only helps if it ends up inside the run we report. So pick the
run first: a run can be made all ones exactly when it contains **at most `k` zeros**. The problem is "longest
window with at most `k` zeros".

**Why the left edge never goes back.** If the window `[L, R]` breaks the rule, then every longer window `[L, R']` with
`R' > R` contains it and breaks the rule too. So once a start `L` fails for some `R`, it fails for all later `R`, and
we can throw it away forever. That's what lets the left pointer only move forward, and makes the whole scan O(n).
**Trace with `k = 2`** (last column = zeros in the window):

When a third zero enters, `L` walks right until a zero has left; ones it passes over are simply dropped. Note
that we never need to decide **which** zeros get patched: all zeros in the final window are.

idea.md:
From every start, extend while the window has at most `k` zeros. Each start's run is the longest from that
start; the best of them is the answer. It restarts the zero count for every start.

lines.text: Each minute as the start of a run. Every index is tried as the left end of the window. Nothing learned from one start is reused for the next, which is exactly the waste the better approaches remove.
Take the next minute if patching it (when it's down) keeps the patches within `k`.
The run from this start has `j − i` minutes.

steps.text: Start 0: the window grows to 0..6 (length 7). Adding 0 at 7 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 1: the window grows to 1..6 (length 6). Adding 0 at 7 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 2: the window grows to 2..6 (length 5). Adding 0 at 7 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 3: the window grows to 3..9 (length 7). Adding 0 at 10 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 4: the window grows to 4..11 (length 8). It reaches the end.
Start 5: the window grows to 5..11 (length 7). It reaches the end.
Starts 6..11 are checked the same way. The longest window starts at 4. In total about 73 cells were re-read, which grows like n²: the same cells are scanned again from every start.
Longest: 8.

walk.title: From each start, extend while at most k down minutes are inside.

limits.md: Restarts the zero count at every start. When `k` is large, each start scans almost the whole log: O(n²).

approaches.title: Window with at most k zeros

idea.md:
Keep a window `[L, R]` and its zero count. Add `status[R]` (zero → count + 1). While the count exceeds
`k`, remove `status[L]` (if it's a zero, count − 1) and advance `L`. Then `R − L + 1` is the longest
patchable run ending at `R`.

**Invariant.** After the loop, `[L, R]` has at most `k` zeros and `L` is the earliest start that allows
it.

lines.text: An empty window with no zeros.
Bring the next element into the window on the right. The window may now break the rule; the next lines repair it. A down minute adds one patch.
With more than `k` zeros the window can't be fixed. Drop minutes from the left until one zero has left. Ones dropped along the way are simply lost from this window.
After the repair, `L … R` is the longest valid window that ends at `R` (no earlier start works). Comparing its length with the best covers every possible right end.
The longest run that can be fully online.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** `R` and `L` each move at most `n` times. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: R adds 1 at 0; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..0. New best: 1.
R adds 1 at 1; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..1. New best: 2.
R adds 0 at 2; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..2. New best: 3.
R adds 0 at 3; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..3. New best: 4.
R adds 1 at 4; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..4. New best: 5.
R adds 1 at 5; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..5. New best: 6.
R adds 1 at 6; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..6. New best: 7.
R adds 0 at 7. That breaks the rule (zeros 3). L moves past 0..2 until it holds again: window 3..7.
R adds 1 at 8; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 3..8.
R adds 1 at 9; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 3..9.
R adds 0 at 10. That breaks the rule (zeros 3). L moves past 3..3 until it holds again: window 4..10.
R adds 1 at 11; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 4..11. New best: 8.
R visited each index once and L only ever moved right, so the pointers made at most 24 moves in total: O(n).
Longest: 8.

walk.title: Grow the window and count its zeros; when there are more than k, move the left edge until one zero leaves.

takeaways.md:
- **"Flip/patch at most k" = window with at most k bad items.**
- Count only the bad items; the window length does the rest.
- The choice of *which* items to change disappears once you pick the window.
